title: Focus quartet without rhythm section
summary: No rhythm section and the brittle sound; the Beaux Arts quartet.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you have this kind of interplay with the concert-
Who was the concertmaster on that? They don't give credit.
Not on the re-issue of Focus; maybe on the original record they did.
That was the Beaux Arts String Quartet, the guy's name was--later he got into the Composers String Quartet--Jerry--I hope he doesn't hear this tape--I'll get it.

There was nothing really that difficult on that. I didn't want to use a rhythm section; that was one of the things I knew I didn't want to use, because I don't like the brittle sound of a rhythm section playing (inaudible).
You can set up a feeling and it is immediately wiped out, and if that's
what you want to do, great, but I didn't want that.

There's a self conscious pacing that jazz has or jazz players have when they go into their "schtick" that doesn't fit with the symphonic jazz concept. I never heard anything that worked along those lines, nothing. So I never really tried it, I never wanted to try it.
